questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Constitutional body and its Nodal Ministry?

options.text: Inter State Council - Ministry of Finance
Attorney general of India - Ministry of Home Affairs
National Commission for SCs - Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Union Public Service Commission - Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Public Service Commission - Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is a Constitutional body responsible for conducting prestigious exams like Civil Services Examination, Indian Forest Service Examination, and others.
 
• It is under the **administrative control of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**, which is headed by the Prime Minister as the Minister-in-charge.
 
• The Ministry provides **administrative support and resources** to UPSC for its functioning.
 
• UPSC was established under **Article 315** of the Indian Constitution, which provides for its composition, appointment, and tenure of members.
 
• The body is independent and insulated from external pressures, ensuring **fair and transparent recruitment** to various government posts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter State Council**

 
 
• The Inter State Council is a Constitutional body established under **Article 263** of the Constitution to facilitate coordination between the Union and State governments.
 
• It is under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of Finance.
 
• The Council is primarily tasked with addressing disputes and fostering cooperative federalism in India.
 
 
 
• **Attorney General of India**
 
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer of India, appointed under **Article 76** of the Constitution.
 
• He/She is not linked to the Ministry of Home Affairs but works as the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**
 
 
• The NCSC is a Constitutional body established under **Article 338** of the Constitution.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, not the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
 
• The Commission safeguards the interests of Scheduled Castes and investigates complaints regarding their rights and privileges.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**
 
 
• This Ministry is the **nodal ministry** for personnel management, including recruitment, training, and capacity building in the Government of India.
 
• It oversees the functioning of Constitutional bodies like UPSC and statutory bodies like the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).
 
• The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) is a key department under this Ministry.

questions.question: When did the Prime Minister of India launch 'Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**October 2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan' was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2024**.
 
• The initiative aims to drive **socio-economic development in tribal areas** with a focus on sustainable growth and self-reliance.
 
• This program aligns with the Indian government’s ongoing efforts to strengthen **tribal welfare and empowerment** under various schemes.
 
• The campaign is named after the revered tribal leader **Birsa Munda**, often referred to as 'Dharti Aaba'.
 
• The Abhiyan emphasizes **education, skill development, health, and livelihood opportunities** for tribal communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Birsa Munda**

 
 
• Birsa Munda was a freedom fighter, religious leader, and folk hero who belonged to the Munda tribe in Jharkhand.
 
• He played a significant role in mobilizing tribal communities against British colonial rule.
 
• Birsa Munda is remembered for his efforts to protect tribal land and culture.
 
• He is referred to as 'Dharti Aaba', meaning 'Father of the Earth'.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Welfare in India**
 
 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is responsible for the implementation of various schemes targeting tribal communities.
 
• Key schemes include **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana**, **Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana**, and **Eklavya Model Residential Schools**.
 
• These programs focus on providing education, healthcare, and livelihood opportunities to tribal populations.
 
 
 
• **Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)**
 
 
• EMRS aims to impart quality education to tribal children in remote areas.
 
• The schools provide free education, accommodation, and meals to students.
 
• The curriculum emphasizes both academics and extracurricular activities to ensure holistic development.
 
 
 
• **Van Dhan Yojana**
 
 
• Van Dhan Yojana is an initiative under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to promote tribal entrepreneurship.
 
• It focuses on the value addition of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) through self-help groups.
 
• The scheme aims to enhance the income of tribal communities by leveraging their traditional knowledge and resources.

questions.question: Which term is used to describe the area of land that drains into a particular river or lake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Watershed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **watershed** is an area of land where all the water drains into a particular river, lake, or other water body.
 
• It includes both surface water (streams, rivers, lakes) and groundwater that flows into the water system.
 
• Watersheds are usually separated by geographical features such as ridges, hills, or mountains.
 
• They play a critical role in water cycle management by collecting, storing, and channeling rainfall and snowmelt to downstream water bodies.
 
• Watershed management is essential for ensuring water quality, preventing floods, and sustaining biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delta**

 
 
• A delta is a landform created at the mouth of a river where it deposits sediments as it flows into a slower-moving or stagnant water body like an ocean, sea, or lake.
 
• Examples include the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta and the Nile Delta.
 
 
 
• **Estuary**
 
 
• An estuary is a coastal area where freshwater from rivers meets and mixes with saltwater from the ocean.
 
• Estuaries are rich in biodiversity and serve as crucial habitats for many aquatic species.
 
 
 
• **Reservoir**
 
 
• A reservoir is an artificial or natural lake used to store water for various purposes such as irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• Examples include the Hirakud Reservoir in India and Lake Mead in the United States.
 
 
 
• **Watershed Management**
 
 
• Watershed management involves sustainable practices to conserve water, prevent erosion, and protect the ecosystem in a watershed area.
 
• It includes activities like afforestation, soil conservation, and rainwater harvesting.

questions.question: Through which Amendment of the Indian Constitution was the Right to Education designated as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **86th Amendment Act**, enacted in 2002, inserted **Article 21A** into the Indian Constitution, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right.
 
• It mandates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• To operationalize this, the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE Act)** was passed in 2009 and came into effect on April 1, 2010.
 
• The amendment also modified **Article 45**, obligating the State to provide early childhood care and education to children below six years of age.
 
• Additionally, it inserted **Article 51A(k)**, specifying that parents or guardians must provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**:

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, ensuring basic rights to all citizens.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts and protect citizens from arbitrary actions by the State.
 
• Articles 12 to 35 cover various Fundamental Rights, including the right to equality, freedom, and education.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**:
 
 
• Introduced by the 86th Amendment, Article 21A provides the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right.
 
• This article ensures that every child aged 6 to 14 years has access to free and compulsory education.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**:
 
 
• The RTE Act is a legislative framework to implement the provisions of Article 21A.
 
• It specifies the responsibilities of the central and state governments, schools, and parents in ensuring universal education.
 
• It also mandates a 25% reservation for economically weaker sections in private schools.
 
 
 
• **Early Childhood Care and Education**:
 
 
• Article 45, as amended, emphasizes the importance of pre-primary education for children below six years of age.
 
• Programs like **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** aim to cater to this need.

questions.question: Which player received the Purple Cap in the IPL 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohammad Shami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohammad Shami**, the Indian fast bowler, won the Purple Cap in IPL 2023 for taking the highest number of wickets in the tournament.
 
• He took a total of **28 wickets** in 17 matches, showcasing his exceptional bowling performance throughout the season.
 
• Shami played a key role in leading his team, the **Gujarat Titans**, to the finals of the IPL 2023.
 
• He maintained an impressive **economy rate of 8.03** and consistently delivered in the powerplay overs.
 
• Shami's dominance in the tournament was a testament to his skill in swinging the ball and executing yorkers effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purple Cap in IPL:**

 
 
• The Purple Cap is awarded to the bowler with the most wickets in a single IPL season.
 
• It was introduced in the inaugural season of IPL in 2008.
 
• The cap is passed on from one bowler to another during the season, depending on who tops the wicket-taker list.
 
• At the end of the tournament, the highest wicket-taker retains the Purple Cap.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat Titans:**
 
 
• The Gujarat Titans are a franchise cricket team that debuted in IPL 2022.
 
• They won the IPL title in their inaugural season under the leadership of Hardik Pandya.
 
• The team is based in Ahmedabad and plays its home matches at the Narendra Modi Stadium.
 
 
 
• **IPL 2023 Overview:**
 
 
• IPL 2023 was the 16th edition of the Indian Premier League.
 
• The tournament featured 10 teams and was played across various venues in India.
 
• The Chennai Super Kings defeated the Gujarat Titans in the final to win their 5th IPL title.
 
 
 
• **Bowling Economy:**
 
 
• Bowling economy rate refers to the average number of runs a bowler concedes per over.
 
• A lower economy rate is considered better and indicates control over the game.
 
• Shami's economy rate of 8.03 in IPL 2023 was commendable, especially in T20 cricket.

questions.question: Sarhul festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sarhul** is a major tribal festival predominantly celebrated in the state of **Jharkhand**.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the **new year for tribal communities** and the advent of the spring season.
 
• It is celebrated by tribes like the **Oraon, Munda, and Ho**, who worship nature and their village deities.
 
• During Sarhul, the tribal communities worship the **Sal tree**, which is considered sacred, and offer its flowers to their deities.
 
• The festival involves traditional music, dance, and rituals that reflect the rich cultural heritage of Jharkhand's tribal population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribal Worship Practices**

 
 
• In tribal culture, nature worship is a central aspect, and festivals like Sarhul are dedicated to expressing gratitude to the environment.
 
• Deities like **
 
 
 
• Sal Tree (Shorea robusta)**
 
 
• The Sal tree holds immense significance in tribal rituals and is considered a symbol of fertility and prosperity.
 
• Its flowers are central to the Sarhul festival and are offered to deities as part of the worship rituals.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Dances and Music**
 
 
• Traditional dance forms such as **Paika** and **Jhumar** are performed during Sarhul.
 
• Musical instruments like the **Mandar** and **Nagara** add rhythm and vibrancy to the celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribal Festivals of Jharkhand**
 
 
• Besides Sarhul, other significant tribal festivals include **Karma Puja**, **Maghe Parab**, and **Baha**.
 
• These festivals emphasize harmony with nature and community bonding.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which state among the following has the highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, **Kerala** has the highest literacy rate among Indian states with a literacy rate of **94.00%**.
 
• Kerala's strong emphasis on education is attributed to the efforts of **missionary organizations** and early societal focus on literacy and schooling.
 
• The state has consistently maintained its leading position in literacy due to its **well-established education infrastructure** and policies.
 
• Kerala's female literacy rate is also the highest in India, reflecting **gender equality in educational access**.
 
• Other states with high literacy rates include Lakshadweep (91.85%) and Mizoram (91.33%), but Kerala remains at the top.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• Literacy rate refers to the percentage of people aged 7 and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.
 
 
 
• **Key Drivers of Kerala's Literacy:**
 
 
• Initiatives like the **Kerala State Literacy Mission** have played a pivotal role in achieving universal literacy.
 
• Strong policies promoting public education and **social reforms** by leaders like Sree Narayana Guru and Ayyankali have contributed significantly.
 
 
 
• **National Literacy Rate (2011):**
 
 
• The overall literacy rate of India, as per the 2011 Census, stands at **74.04%** with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Global Literacy:**
 
 
• India's literacy rate, though improving, still lags behind the global average of **86.3%** (as per UNESCO data).
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments:**
 
 
• The **New Education Policy 2020** emphasizes universal foundational literacy and numeracy to improve India's literacy landscape.

questions.question: Which member of the phylum Porifera is the oldest metazoan group still existing on our planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sponges**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sponges (phylum Porifera) are considered the **oldest metazoan group** still existing on Earth, dating back to the Precambrian era, approximately 600 million years ago.
 
• They are simple multicellular organisms that lack tissues, organs, and a nervous system but possess specialized cells for various functions like feeding and reproduction.
 
• Sponges rely on a water canal system to filter feed, making them highly efficient filter feeders in aquatic ecosystems.
 
• Their fossil records suggest that they played a significant role in the evolution of early marine ecosystems and are considered a cornerstone in the study of evolutionary biology.
 
• Sponges are exclusively aquatic, with the majority being marine, although some freshwater species also exist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Porifera:**

 
 
• Porifera, commonly known as sponges, derive their name from the Latin word "porus" (pore) and "ferre" (to bear), referring to their porous bodies.
 
• They exhibit **asymmetrical or radial symmetry** and are sessile as adults.
 
• Sponges have a skeleton made of spicules (calcareous or siliceous) or spongin fibers, providing structural support.
 
 
 
• **Water Canal System:**
 
 
• Sponges use a specialized canal system comprising ostia (pores), spongocoel (central cavity), and osculum (excurrent opening) to circulate water for feeding, respiration, and excretion.
 
• This system is driven by the beating of flagella in specialized cells called choanocytes.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Strategies:**
 
 
• Sponges reproduce both sexually (via gametes) and asexually (budding, fragmentation, or gemmules).
 
• They are hermaphroditic, meaning an individual can produce both eggs and sperm, although cross-fertilization is common.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Sponges serve as habitat-forming species, providing shelter for various marine organisms.
 
• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling by filtering large volumes of water and capturing microscopic particles.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:**
 
 
• Sponges are considered basal metazoans, representing an evolutionary link between unicellular and multicellular life forms.
 
• They offer insights into the origin and evolution of multicellular animals due to their simple body structure and cellular organization.

questions.question: A serve must pass the short service line, which is 1.98 m (6.5ft) from the net. The ‘Short Service Line’ is a line in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Badminton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Short Service Line' is an essential marking on the badminton court, located 1.98 m (6.5 ft) from the net.
 
• In badminton, the serve must cross the short service line to be considered valid during play.
 
• The short service line is part of the court's design, ensuring fair play and regulating the serving area.
 
• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF), which specifies the court dimensions, including the placement of the short service line.
 
• Correct positioning and serving techniques in relation to the short service line are crucial for a competitive game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Badminton Court Dimensions:**

 
 
• The full length of the badminton court is 13.4 m (44 ft), and the width is 6.1 m (20 ft) for doubles and 5.18 m (17 ft) for singles.
 
• The net is placed at a height of 1.55 m (5 ft 1 in) at the edges and 1.524 m (5 ft) at the center.
 
 
 
• **Serving Rules in Badminton:**
 
 
• The serve must be delivered below the waist height and with the racket shaft pointing downward.
 
• The server must stand within the service area and ensure the shuttle crosses the short service line for a valid serve.
 
 
 
• **Types of Service in Badminton:**
 
 
• Common types include high serve, low serve, flick serve, and drive serve, each suited for different strategies.
 
• The choice of serve depends on the player's position and the opponent's weaknesses.
 
 
 
• **Badminton World Federation (BWF):**
 
 
• Established in 1934, BWF is the international governing body for the sport of badminton.
 
• It oversees major tournaments like the World Championships and the Thomas and Uber Cups.

questions.question: Which sector contributes more to the GDP, at the higher level of development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Service**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The service sector is the largest contributor to GDP in most developed economies, including India, accounting for over **50% of the GDP** at higher levels of development.
 
• This sector encompasses industries such as **banking, finance, education, healthcare, information technology (IT), and tourism**, among others.
 
• India's service sector has shown exponential growth over the years due to **urbanization, technological advancements, and globalization**.
 
• In advanced economies, the shift from manufacturing and agriculture to services is termed as **economic structural transformation**.
 
• As of recent data, India's service sector accounts for approximately **54% of its GDP**, showcasing its dominant role in economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Structural Transformation:** It refers to the shift in economic activity from primary sectors like agriculture to secondary (manufacturing) and tertiary (services) sectors as economies develop.
 
• **Agriculture Sector Contribution:** In developing economies, agriculture usually plays a significant role in GDP, but its share declines as economies mature and shift focus to services and industry.
 
• **Industry Sector Contribution:** The industrial sector typically peaks during the mid-development phase before the service sector dominates in advanced stages.
 
• **Global Service Economy Trends:** Countries like the USA, UK, and Germany have service sectors contributing over 70% of their GDP, driven by advancements in technology and digitalization.
 
• **India's IT Sector:** The IT and software services industry is a key driver of India's service sector, contributing significantly to exports and employment generation.

questions.question: The period when we find environmental changes, beginning about 12,000 years ago till about 10,000 years ago, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesolithic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mesolithic period, also known as the **Middle Stone Age**, spanned roughly from 12,000 to 10,000 years ago.
 
• This period marks the transition between the Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) and Neolithic (New Stone Age) periods.
 
• It was characterized by significant **environmental changes** due to the end of the last Ice Age, leading to a warmer climate.
 
• Humans in the Mesolithic period began using more sophisticated tools, known as **microliths**, which were small, sharp stone tools.
 
• During this time, people adopted a **semi-nomadic lifestyle**, combining hunting, fishing, and gathering with early forms of agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palaeolithic Period:**

 
 
• The Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) lasted from about 2.5 million years ago to around 10,000 BCE.
 
• Humans were hunter-gatherers during this period and used rudimentary tools made of stone.
 
• Cave paintings and other forms of early art emerged during the late Palaeolithic.
 
 
 
• **Microliths:**
 
 
• Microliths were small, geometrically shaped stone tools used during the Mesolithic period.
 
• These tools were often attached to wooden or bone handles to create arrows, spears, and other composite tools.
 
 
 
• **Neolithic Period:**
 
 
• The Neolithic period (New Stone Age) followed the Mesolithic, beginning around 10,000 BCE.
 
• It was marked by the advent of agriculture, domestication of animals, and permanent settlements.
 
• Humans began using polished stone tools and developed pottery and weaving techniques.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Changes:**
 
 
• The end of the Ice Age led to warmer climates, rising sea levels, and the formation of new ecosystems.
 
• These changes influenced the availability of plants and animals, prompting humans to adapt their subsistence strategies.

questions.question: Which of the following Gharanas of Kathak was Pandit Ishwari Prasad related to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Ishwari Prasad is traditionally regarded as the originator of the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak.
 
• According to legend, he received divine inspiration from Lord Krishna in a dream, which guided him to develop Kathak as a devotional art form.
 
• He lived during the 18th century, a time when Kathak was transitioning from temple rituals to court performances.
 
• His descendants continued the tradition, and the Lucknow Gharana became known for its graceful movements, expressive abhinaya (facial expressions), and refined gestures.
 
• The Lucknow Gharana, through Ishwari Prasad’s lineage, greatly influenced the aesthetic and emotional aspects of Kathak, distinguishing it from other gharanas like Jaipur and Banaras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak:**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its storytelling approach.
 
• The term "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," which means story.
 
• It originated in North India and evolved from temple dances and later incorporated Mughal influences.
 
 
 
• **Banaras Gharana:**
 
 
• Banaras Gharana is deeply rooted in the devotional aspect of Kathak and emphasizes expressions and spirituality.
 
• Its compositions often include devotional themes centered around Lord Krishna and other Hindu deities.
 
 
 
• **Other Kathak Gharanas:**
 
 
• **Lucknow Gharana:** Known for its emphasis on elegance, grace, and emotive storytelling.
 
• **Jaipur Gharana:** Famous for its vigorous footwork and complex rhythmic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Bol:**
 
 
• Bol refers to syllables that represent rhythmic patterns in Indian classical dance and music.
 
• Natwari Bol is a unique feature of Banaras Gharana, focusing on rhythmic expressions associated with Lord Krishna's dance.

questions.question: On which date was Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st October 2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY)** was launched on **1st October 2020** to boost employment in the formal sector.
 
• It aimed to incentivize employers for the creation of new employment opportunities by reducing the financial burden of EPF contributions.
 
• The scheme was part of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat package announced by the Government of India to revive the economy post-COVID-19.
 
• Under ABRY, the government bears both the **employee's and employer's share** of EPF contributions (24% of wages) for two years for new employees in establishments with up to 1,000 employees.
 
• For establishments with more than 1,000 employees, the government pays only the **employee's EPF contribution (12%)** for two years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **EPF (Employees' Provident Fund)**

 
 
• A retirement benefits scheme regulated by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
 
• It requires both employers and employees to contribute 12% of the employee's basic salary and dearness allowance.
 
• Funds accumulated in EPF accounts can be withdrawn upon retirement or under special circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan**
 
 
• A comprehensive economic package announced by the Government of India in May 2020 to combat the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• It focused on making India self-reliant by strengthening local manufacturing, supply chains, and infrastructure.
 
• Key pillars include economy, infrastructure, technology-driven systems, demography, and demand.
 
 
 
• **Impact of ABRY**
 
 
• ABRY has contributed to the formalization of jobs and provided social security benefits to workers.
 
• It has promoted the registration of new employees under EPFO, ensuring long-term savings for workers.
 
• The scheme played a crucial role in supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) during the economic slowdown caused by COVID-19.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for ABRY**
 
 
• New employees earning wages less than Rs. 15,000 per month were eligible under the scheme.
 
• Existing EPF members who had lost their jobs during the pandemic and were re-employed were also eligible.

questions.question: 4In the context of Keynesian economics, what would be an ideal government response to an overheated economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Implement contractionary fiscal policies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Contractionary fiscal policies involve reducing government spending or increasing taxes to curb excessive demand in the economy.
 
• These policies aim to slow down inflationary pressures in an overheated economy by reducing aggregate demand.
 
• Increased taxes reduce disposable income, discouraging consumer spending and cooling down demand-driven inflation.
 
• Lower government spending reduces the injection of money into the economy, thereby controlling inflation and stabilizing the economic cycle.
 
• Such measures help achieve a sustainable growth rate while maintaining price stability and avoiding economic disruptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keynesian Economics:**

 
 
• Developed by economist John Maynard Keynes, this framework emphasizes the role of aggregate demand in driving economic output.
 
• It advocates government intervention in managing economic cycles to mitigate recessions and overheating.
 
 
 
• **Overheated Economy:**
 
 
• An economic condition characterized by high inflation, excessive demand, and unsustainable growth rates.
 
• Indicators include rising prices, labor shortages, and pressure on production capacities.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Control Measures:**
 
 
• Besides fiscal policy, monetary tools like increasing interest rates are used to combat inflation.
 
• Central banks play a critical role in implementing monetary policies to complement fiscal efforts.
 
 
 
• **Aggregate Demand:**
 
 
• The total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given time and price level.
 
• It is influenced by factors such as consumer spending, investment, government spending, and net exports.

questions.question: Which of the following songs was NOT sung by Kishore Kumar?

options.text: Kora Kagaz Tha Yeh Man Mera
Yaari Hai Imam Mera Yaar Meri Zindagi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yaari Hai Imaan Mera Yaar Meri Zindagi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yaari Hai Imaan Mera Yaar Meri Zindagi** is a popular song from the movie **Zanjeer (1973)**, sung by the legendary playback singer **Manna Dey**.
 
• Kishore Kumar was not the singer of this song; it was beautifully rendered by Manna Dey, known for his classical touch.
 
• The song was composed by the famous music director duo **Kalyanji-Anandji** and written by lyricist **Gulshan Bawra**.
 
• Kishore Kumar, though widely celebrated for his versatility, did not sing this particular track, which was more suited to Manna Dey's vocal style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kishore Kumar**

 
 
• Kishore Kumar was one of India's most iconic playback singers, famous for his versatility in singing romantic, melancholic, and upbeat songs.
 
• He lent his voice to numerous evergreen tracks including **Gaata Rahe Mera Dil**, **Kora Kagaz Tha Yeh Man Mera**, and **Dekha Ek Khwaab**.
 
• Kishore Kumar was also a renowned actor, composer, lyricist, and filmmaker in Indian cinema.
 
 
 
• **Manna Dey**
 
 
• Manna Dey was a legendary playback singer known for his classical expertise and versatility across genres.
 
• He sang iconic songs like **Yaari Hai Imaan Mera Yaar Meri Zindagi**, **Ae Mere Zohra Jabeen**, and **Laga Chunari Mein Daag**.
 
• He received numerous accolades, including the **Padma Shri** and **Padma Bhushan** for his contributions to Indian music.
 
 
 
• **Music of Zanjeer**
 
 
• The movie **Zanjeer**, released in 1973, marked a turning point in Indian cinema and introduced the "angry young man" persona of Amitabh Bachchan.
 
• The soundtrack was composed by **Kalyanji-Anandji**, who were known for delivering memorable melodies.
 
• Lyrics were penned by **Gulshan Bawra**, contributing to the timeless appeal of the movie's songs.

questions.question: In which year was Narayanan EP, related to Theyyam ritual art form of dance and music, awarded the Padma Shri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2022**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Narayanan EP, a practitioner of the traditional Kerala ritual art form **Theyyam**, was awarded the **Padma Shri in 2022**.
 
• The Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian award and is conferred upon individuals for their distinguished contributions in various fields.
 
• **Theyyam** is a ritualistic dance and art form performed in the northern districts of Kerala, particularly Kannur and Kasaragod.
 
• Narayanan EP was recognized for his exceptional dedication to **preserving and promoting Theyyam**, which blends dance, music, and symbolic expressions of divinity.
 
• The Padma Awards, including Padma Shri, are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day and serve to acknowledge contributions in fields such as art, literature, social work, and more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theyyam**

 
 
• Theyyam is a centuries-old ritualistic and theatrical art form that is deeply rooted in the culture of northern Kerala.
 
• It is believed to represent divine manifestations and is performed in temples and sacred groves.
 
• Performers wear elaborate costumes, face paint, and headdresses, creating a striking visual spectacle.
 
• The dance involves storytelling, invoking gods, and seeking blessings, reflecting the region's folklore and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• The Padma Awards consist of three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• These awards are given by the Government of India to individuals for excellence in various fields such as art, literature, science, and public service.
 
• The selection process involves recommendations from the public and scrutiny by the Padma Awards Committee.
 
• The awards are presented by the President of India at a ceremonial function held in Rashtrapati Bhavan.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Cultural Heritage**
 
 
• Kerala is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, with art forms like Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and Theyyam.
 
• It is often called "God's Own Country" due to its lush landscapes and spiritual traditions.
 
• Traditional festivals such as Onam and Vishu showcase Kerala's vibrant cultural practices.
 
• The state has a strong focus on preserving its indigenous art forms through various cultural initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Ritualistic Art**
 
 
• Ritualistic art like Theyyam serves as a medium to connect communities with their spiritual and cultural roots.
 
• It often conveys moral stories, religious values, and social messages.
 
• Such art forms are instrumental in preserving oral traditions and folk narratives.
 
• They play a crucial role in fostering cultural identity and continuity across generations.

questions.question: On 20 July 1969, with whom did American astronaut Neil Armstrong became the first human to land on the moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Edwin Aldrin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On **20 July 1969**, Neil Armstrong and Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin became the first humans to land on the Moon during NASA's **Apollo 11 mission**.
 
• Neil Armstrong was the first to step onto the lunar surface, followed by Edwin Aldrin. Armstrong famously said, "**That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind**."
 
• The **Lunar Module (LM), named "Eagle,"** was used to land on the Moon's surface, while the Command Module "Columbia" remained in lunar orbit.
 
• Michael Collins, the third astronaut on the Apollo 11 mission, piloted the Command Module and did not descend to the Moon.
 
• The Apollo 11 mission marked a significant milestone in human history and established the United States' dominance in the **Space Race** against the Soviet Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apollo Program:**

 
 
• The Apollo program was initiated by NASA in the 1960s to land humans on the Moon and safely return them to Earth.
 
• Apollo 11 was the first successful lunar landing mission, followed by six more lunar missions.
 
• The program contributed significantly to advancing space exploration and related technologies.
 
 
 
• **Lunar Module (LM):**
 
 
• The LM was a spacecraft specifically designed for landing on the Moon and returning to lunar orbit.
 
• It consisted of two stages: the descent stage for landing and the ascent stage for returning to orbit.
 
 
 
• **Space Race:**
 
 
• The Space Race was a Cold War-era competition between the United States and the Soviet Union for dominance in space exploration.
 
• The Soviet Union achieved the first human spaceflight with Yuri Gagarin in 1961, while the U.S. achieved the first lunar landing in 1969.
 
 
 
• **Moon Facts:**
 
 
• The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and is about 384,400 km away from Earth.
 
• Its surface is covered with craters, mountains, and plains formed by ancient volcanic activity and meteorite impacts.

questions.question: As of September 2024, Brig. (Dr.) BD Mishra (Retd.) is the Lieutenant Governor of which of the following union territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Brig. (Dr.) BD Mishra (Retd.) was appointed as the **Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh** in February 2023.
 
• The Lieutenant Governor (LG) is the **administrative head** of the Union Territory (UT) and represents the President of India in the region.
 
• BD Mishra succeeded Radha Krishna Mathur as the LG of Ladakh, becoming the **second person to hold the position** since Ladakh became a Union Territory in October 2019.
 
• Prior to this role, BD Mishra served as the **Governor of Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• The appointment of BD Mishra as LG is significant in the context of Ladakh's strategic importance and developmental priorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Territory of Ladakh:**

 
 
• Ladakh became a Union Territory on **31 October 2019**, following the bifurcation of Jammu & Kashmir under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019.
 
• It consists of two districts: **Leh and Kargil**.
 
• The UT does not have a legislative assembly and is directly governed by the Lieutenant Governor and the central government.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lieutenant Governor:**
 
 
• The Lieutenant Governor acts as the **representative of the President of India** in Union Territories without a legislature.
 
• The LG has administrative, executive, and ceremonial responsibilities, particularly in regions with unique governance structures like Ladakh.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Ladakh:**
 
 
• Ladakh shares borders with China (Tibet Autonomous Region) and Pakistan (Gilgit-Baltistan).
 
• It holds significant importance in terms of **national security** and geopolitics, particularly due to the ongoing India-China border disputes.
 
 
 
• **Developmental Challenges in Ladakh:**
 
 
• Ladakh faces unique challenges such as **harsh climatic conditions, limited infrastructure, and ecological sensitivity**.
 
• The Indian government has been focusing on improving connectivity, tourism, and sustainable development in the region.

questions.question: What does the term 'commerce' mainly refer to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distribution of goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Commerce** primarily refers to the activities involved in the **exchange and distribution** of goods and services.
 
• It is a major branch of business that focuses on the movement of goods from producers to consumers via trade, transport, and related services.
 
• Commerce includes all processes that facilitate transactions such as **sales, marketing, logistics, and financial systems**.
 
• The ultimate goal of commerce is to ensure that goods and services are **available to consumers at the right time and place**.
 
• It acts as a bridge between **production and consumption**, ensuring smooth economic activities in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade**

 
 
• Trade is a subset of commerce and involves the **buying and selling of goods and services.**
 
• It can be conducted at various levels, such as **local, national, and international trade.**
 
• Trade plays a critical role in commerce by enabling the flow of goods across regions and countries.
 
 
 
• **Logistics**
 
 
• Logistics refers to the process of **planning, implementing, and controlling** the efficient transportation and storage of goods.
 
• It ensures the timely delivery of products to consumers and businesses.
 
• Modern logistics heavily relies on technology such as **tracking systems and automated warehouses.**
 
 
 
• **Supply Chain**
 
 
• The supply chain encompasses the **entire network** involved in producing and delivering a product or service.
 
• It includes suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and end consumers.
 
• Effective supply chain management is essential for optimizing costs and ensuring efficiency in commerce.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Commerce**
 
 
• Commerce contributes significantly to a nation's GDP by facilitating **trade and economic activities.**
 
• It creates job opportunities in sectors such as transportation, retail, finance, and marketing.
 
• Commerce also helps in the **globalization of businesses**, connecting markets across the world.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the British government publish the White Paper based on the recommendations of the Third Round Table Conference?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1933**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The British government published the **White Paper** in 1933 based on the recommendations of the **Third Round Table Conference**.
 
• The White Paper served as the basis for the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which aimed to introduce provincial autonomy and reforms in British India's governance system.
 
• The **Third Round Table Conference** was held in London from November 1932 to December 1932, focusing on constitutional reforms for India.
 
• Unlike the previous conferences, the **Third Round Table Conference** saw limited participation from Indian political leaders and focused heavily on British perspectives.
 
• The White Paper outlined proposals for reforms, but it faced criticism from Indian leaders who viewed it as inadequate and biased toward British interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Round Table Conferences**

 
 
• Three Round Table Conferences were held between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• The **First Round Table Conference (1930)** saw participation from British officials, Indian princes, and other representatives, but no Congress leaders attended.
 
• The **Second Round Table Conference (1931)** included Mahatma Gandhi as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The **Third Round Table Conference (1932)** had fewer Indian representatives and was largely dominated by British officials.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• It was based on the recommendations of the White Paper published in 1933.
 
• The act introduced provincial autonomy and a federal structure for governance.
 
• It marked a significant step toward self-governance but was criticized for retaining excessive power in British hands.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the White Paper**
 
 
• The White Paper was criticized for failing to address India's demand for complete independence.
 
• It led to further alienation of Indian political leaders, particularly the Indian National Congress.
 
• It served as a precursor to the Government of India Act, 1935, which became the framework for British India's governance until independence.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures in the Round Table Conferences**
 
 
• British Prime Ministers **Ramsay MacDonald** and **Stanley Baldwin** played pivotal roles in hosting and moderating the conferences.
 
• Indian representatives included leaders from various communities, such as **B.R. Ambedkar**, **Tej Bahadur Sapru**, and **Sir Muhammad Iqbal**.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference was a notable event, focusing on India's demand for independence.
